picks.title: Book Marketing: AI, Book Discoverability and Resilience, with Ricardo Fayet
picks.excerpt: Reedsy's Ricardo Fayet argues AI search engines are rewriting book discoverability: readers now ask conversational questions instead of typing keywords, so books get surfaced by review volume and cross-web mentions rather than metadata keywords. Authors are told to build an 'internet footprint' across Goodreads, Reddit and reviews so LLMs can recommend them.
picks.rationale: The most directly actionable item in the pool — it says the keyword-and-metadata playbook authors have run for a decade is now the wrong lever, and names what replaces it: review volume and mentions an LLM can actually cite.

picks.title: Guest Post — AI Can Find the Article. Can It Tell Which Version It Used?
picks.excerpt: Patrick Hargitt and Steve Smith argue that AI retrieval tools can locate a paper but rarely know which version they read, and that persistent identifiers alone don't fix it. They call for semantic versioning and provenance metadata baked into publishing workflows so AI-mediated reading stays traceable.
picks.rationale: A concrete failure in AI reading that a publisher can fix on their own side this quarter — versioning and provenance metadata — rather than another abstract call for trustworthy AI.

picks.title: McGraw Hill touts AI in improving first-quarter results
picks.excerpt: McGraw Hill now runs eight live AI learning tools with 7.5 million active users and three more launching this fiscal year. Its AI Reader — which lets students highlight passages inside an e-book and self-quiz — logged 63 million learning interactions across 2.6 million students since fall 2024.
picks.rationale: Rare hard numbers instead of sentiment: 7.5M users and 63M logged interactions turn 'AI in publishing' into a measured product line, and give anyone pitching AI reading features an actual benchmark.

picks.title: Story Hacker OS — a first look at AI that makes you a better fiction writer
picks.excerpt: A first look at Story Hacker OS, an AI writing environment that helps novelists build stronger stories using genre templates, trope libraries and a book builder while keeping the author in control of craft decisions — framed as AI making you a better fiction writer, not replacing you.
picks.rationale: A named, shippable tool rather than a think piece, and it takes the opposite bet from prose generators: structure and trope scaffolding assisted by AI, final craft calls left with the author.

picks.title: The Ultimate Automated Author Experience — a first look at the full stack
picks.excerpt: Elizabeth Ann West and Stacey Anderson preview 'The Ultimate Automated Author Experience,' a big-picture roadmap for an end-to-end AI-assisted authoring stack — drafting, revision and production — coming this fall from Future Fiction Academy.
picks.rationale: Marks the shift from single-purpose AI writing tools to a whole authoring pipeline with a dated arrival, which is the shape authors will have to plan their workflow around this fall.
